input.task: How many entries does the ledger report as loaded?

provenance: PR #70 R1. ADR-035 Decision 2 gave the loop-mode drill an element-scoped capture, and Playwright's `locator.screenshot()` performs an actionability check that scrolls the element into view first. On a page whose coordinate frames are the only thing that moves that is harmless — the next viewport shot is taken after the scroll — but on a lazy-load / infinite-scroll page it is not: looking closer LOADS content the model never acted for, and the run records it as a step that changed nothing, because `observe` sits in `agent.READ_ONLY_ACTIONS` so `page_changed` stays null. An action classified read-only that produces a state change is the shape this repo grades against, so it is graded rather than declared: the drill target is a section 1400px down, outside the 720px viewport, and the step after it reads a status the fixture rewrites on the first scroll event. Watched red on 2026-08-28 against the capture as ADR-035 first shipped it (`loc.screenshot()`): `answer` came back '9 entries loaded' against this case's '3 entries loaded'. Green once the capture became a viewport shot clipped to the element's box, which moves nothing — and which, for an element outside the viewport, declines to capture at all rather than scrolling to it, the same best-effort degrade Decision 1 already takes when a capture fails. PR #70 R9 adds the `driver_screenshots` conjunct: the answer alone left a build that dropped element crops entirely, or emitted one for an off-screen element without scrolling, shipping GREEN on the case written to catch that. `false` at the drill turn pins the absent crop and the two `"viewport"` entries pin that the turns either side keep theirs. Watched red on its own, with the crop emitted for the off-screen element via a full-page clip that does not scroll: `checks {status: true, verdict: true, trace_actions: true, driver_screenshots: false}` — the conjunct discriminates without leaning on the answer.

triage.note: model-input capture is not a free observation; anything that scrolls to take it can change what the run reads next.
